title: Topographic Map Symbols
description: The official USGS legend for topographic map symbols - contours, boundaries, vegetation, hydrography, transportation, and structures - the standard reference for reading a USGS topo map.
provenance_notes: Source: https://pubs.usgs.gov/gip/TopographicMapSymbols/topomapsymbols.pdf - retrieved 2026-09-02. USGS-authored work of the US federal government, public domain under 17 U.S.C. Sec. 105 (confirmed against USGS's own published copyright policy, usgs.gov/information-policies-and-instructions/copyrights-and-credits: "USGS-authored or produced data and information are considered to be in the U.S. Public Domain"). No non-USGS third-party imagery involved - this is a symbols legend, not a photo collection.

title: NIST Time and Frequency Services (NIST Special Publication 432)
description: NIST's comprehensive reference on time and frequency measurement, calibration, and broadcast services (WWV/WWVB, GPS timing, NTP) - the authoritative technical background behind the time-confidence concepts this device's own Field Tools/status pages already surface.
source: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
provenance_notes: Source: https://www.nist.gov/document/sp432-02pdf (resolves to nist.gov/system/files/documents/calibrations/sp432-02.pdf) - retrieved 2026-09-02. NIST Special Publication series, authored by NIST employees (Lombardi et al.) as part of their official duties - public domain under 17 U.S.C. Sec. 105 (confirmed against NIST's own copyright policy page, nist.gov/open: works of NIST employees are not subject to US copyright; the Standard Reference Data Act exception does not apply to this narrative technical publication).

title: Sky Watcher Cloud Chart
description: A visual cloud-identification chart (cirrus, cumulus, stratus, and their combinations/altitudes) for identifying cloud types by sight - useful alongside this device's severe-weather monitoring guidance.
provenance_notes: Source: https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/sites/default/files/sky-watcher-cloud-chart-noaa-nasa-english-version.pdf - retrieved 2026-09-02. Joint publication of two US federal agencies (NOAA and NASA) - public domain under 17 U.S.C. Sec. 105 (confirmed against NOAA's own copyright policy, library.noaa.gov: works of the US federal government are public domain; the caveat about non-federal co-authors, e.g. universities/Cooperative Institutes, does not apply here since both co-authoring agencies are federal).

title: Make Water Safe During an Emergency
description: CDC fact sheet on making water safe to drink after an emergency or disaster - boiling, chemical disinfection, and filtering, with the important limitation that fuel/chemical/radioactive contamination cannot be fixed by any of these methods.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
provenance_notes: Source: https://www.cdc.gov/water-emergency/media/pdfs/make-water-safe-during-emergency-p.pdf - retrieved 2026-09-02. CDC-authored public health fact sheet, work of the US federal government, public domain under 17 U.S.C. Sec. 105 (confirmed against CDC's own copyright guidance: "Most of the information on the CDC and ATSDR websites is not subject to copyright, is in the public domain" - the caveat about contractor/grantee-developed or third-party-licensed material does not apply to this agency-authored fact sheet).

title: Family Emergency Communication Plan
description: FEMA/Ready.gov's full fillable family emergency communication plan - household contact info, out-of-town contact, meeting places, school/work emergency plans, and important medical/insurance information in one printable document.
provenance_notes: Source: https://www.ready.gov/sites/default/files/2020-03/family-emergency-communication-planning-document.pdf - retrieved 2026-09-02. FEMA-authored preparedness publication, public domain under 17 U.S.C. Sec. 105 (confirmed against FEMA's own copyright policy: "Most material on FEMA.gov is free of copyright and may be copied and distributed without permission"; Ready Campaign publications are explicitly made available for free public download/reproduction).

title: Food and Water Safety During Power Outages and Floods
description: FDA consumer factsheet on keeping food and water safe during a power outage or flood - refrigerator/freezer safe-time thresholds, a food-safety decision guide (when to keep vs. discard), and water safety/treatment basics. A different USDA FSIS candidate on this same general topic was blocked by durable HTTP 403 bot protection; this FDA document independently covers the same subject and was confirmed directly accessible and public domain.
provenance_notes: Source: https://www.fda.gov/media/72124/download (from the FDA page 'Food and Water Safety During Power Outages and Floods') - retrieved 2026-09-02. FDA-authored consumer factsheet, work of the US federal government, public domain under 17 U.S.C. Sec. 105 (confirmed against FDA's own website policy: 'the contents of the FDA website...are not copyrighted. They are in the public domain and may be republished, reprinted and otherwise used freely by anyone without the need to obtain permission from FDA' - no third-party/licensed content indicated for this plain agency-authored factsheet).

title: First Aid (FM 4-25.11 / NTRP 4-02.1 / AFMAN 44-163(I))
description: The joint US military field manual on first aid - full step-by-step procedures with illustrations for airway/breathing/bleeding control, shock, fractures/splinting, burns, cold/heat injury, bites/stings, and evacuation/transport techniques. Addresses the visual-diagram gap the First Aid Reference page's own audit flagged (CPR hand position, recovery position, splinting, etc.) with an authoritative, fully redistributable original source, after Red Cross material was found not to be freely redistributable.
source: Headquarters, Departments of the Army, the Navy, and the Air Force, and Commandant, Marine Corps (joint US military publication)
provenance_notes: Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:FM_4-25.11_(FM_21-11)_First_Aid_(Change_1).pdf (direct file: upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/01/FM_4-25.11_%28FM_21-11%29_First_Aid_%28Change_1%29.pdf) - retrieved 2026-09-02. A US Department of Defense work of the federal government, public domain under 17 U.S.C. Sec. 105 (Wikimedia Commons' file page tags it PD-USGov-Military-Army/Navy/Air Force/Marines; the manual's own cover states 'Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited'). Verified 227 pages, 2,621,944 bytes, matching Wikimedia Commons' listed file size exactly - not a truncated/partial copy.

title: Reduce Your Smoke Exposure (Wildfire Smoke Factsheet)
description: EPA factsheet on reducing exposure to wildfire smoke - indoor/outdoor precautions, air cleaners, and who is at greater risk, developed through interagency collaboration including the US Forest Service.
provenance_notes: Source: https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2026-06/reduce-smoke-exposure-factsheet.pdf - retrieved 2026-09-02. EPA-authored public health factsheet, work of the US federal government, public domain under 17 U.S.C. Sec. 105 (confirmed against EPA's own copyright policy framework - covers works of the US Government distinctly from contractor/grantee-produced or third-party content, and this is a plain agency-authored factsheet, not either of those exceptions). Developed with US Forest Service/CDC/other agency input per EPA's own wildfire smoke guide materials, but authored/published by EPA.
